title: 2 Chronicles 29:12–19
context: Levites from each clan, and from the families of the singers, gather their brothers, sanctify themselves, and cleanse the LORD’s house. The priests carry the uncleanness from the inner part to the court, and the Levites take it to the brook Kidron. In sixteen days the work is done, and they report that the altar, the table, and the vessels Ahaz threw away have been sanctified. Both traditions read this as shared ground about restored worship.

verses.text: Then the Levites arose: Mahath, the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; and of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah;
verses.arminianNotes: Levites from the clans of Kohath, Merari, and Gershon arise. Arminian readers see individuals stepping forward in response to the king’s call, each named as a willing participant.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that all three Levitical clans are represented. The list shows the whole tribe joined in the work, in keeping with the divisions described in the law and in 1 Chronicles 23.

verses.text: and of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
verses.arminianNotes: The sons of Elizaphan and of Asaph join the work. Arminian readers note that the singers’ families take part alongside the clans, so that those who lead praise also share in cleansing.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that Elizaphan was a leader among the Kohathites (Numbers 3:30), and Asaph was among David’s appointed musicians (1 Chronicles 25:1). The Chronicler honors both lines.

verses.text: and of the sons of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.arminianNotes: The sons of Heman and Jeduthun complete the list. Arminian readers see the families of musicians willingly giving themselves to the less glamorous labor of cleansing the house.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Heman and Jeduthun, with Asaph, were the three families David set over the music (1 Chronicles 25:1). Their presence anticipates the worship that will follow the cleansing.

verses.text: They gathered their brothers, sanctified themselves, and went in, according to the commandment of the king by the LORD’s words, to cleanse the LORD’s house.
verses.arminianNotes: They gathered their brothers, sanctified themselves, and cleansed the house according to the king’s command by the LORD’s words. Arminian readers see willing obedience joined to the authority of God’s word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the phrase by the LORD’s words, grounding the king’s command in God’s revealed will. Reform follows Scripture, not mere royal preference or political advantage.

verses.text: The priests went into the inner part of the LORD’s house to cleanse it, and brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the LORD’s temple into the court of the LORD’s house. The Levites took it from there to carry it out to the brook Kidron.
verses.arminianNotes: The priests bring the uncleanness out of the inner part, and the Levites carry it to the brook Kidron. Arminian readers see a careful division of labor, each group doing the part assigned to it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that only priests enter the inner part, honoring the law’s distinctions of holiness. The Kidron, outside the city, receives what had defiled God’s house.

verses.text: Now they began on the first day of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the LORD’s porch. They sanctified the LORD’s house in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
verses.arminianNotes: They worked eight days to reach the porch and eight more to finish the house, ending on the sixteenth day. Arminian readers see persistence in a task that took patience and sustained effort.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the precise dating, which the Chronicler records with care. The timing will matter for the Passover in the next chapter, which could not be kept in the first month.

verses.text: Then they went in to Hezekiah the king within the palace and said, “We have cleansed all the LORD’s house, including the altar of burnt offering with all its vessels, and the table of show bread with all its vessels.
verses.arminianNotes: They report that they have cleansed the altar of burnt offering and the table of show bread with all their vessels. Arminian readers see faithful work completed and reported honestly to the king.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the altar and table are central to the restored service. The report marks the end of preparation and the beginning of renewed worship.

verses.text: Moreover, we have prepared and sanctified all the vessels which King Ahaz threw away in his reign when he was unfaithful. Behold, they are before the LORD’s altar.”
verses.arminianNotes: They have prepared and sanctified the vessels King Ahaz threw away when he was unfaithful. Arminian readers see what was discarded restored, a picture of renewal after a season of neglect.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Ahaz’s unfaithfulness is named directly. The restored vessels before the altar recall 28:24, where he cut them in pieces, and show God’s worship rebuilt.
